summary.business: The Company designs and manufactures passive connectivity products across two verticals: Telecommunication (fibre-optic and copper network infrastructure for telecom service providers, including rural fibre rollout) and Enterprise/IT-Networking (Office Network and Data Centre connectivity products such as enclosures, cords, cables and racking systems). Its high-density fibre portfolio and Data-Centre-focused hardware serve telecom operators as well as customers across BFSI, Healthcare, Pharma, Defense, Education, E-commerce and Manufacturing verticals.

currentContext.strategies: Strategic focus on expanding the fibre-optic network across urban and rural markets, viewed as critical to India's Digital India vision and to bridging the urban-rural digital divide|Focus remains on providing high-quality, reliable and affordable passive products for copper, Modules and fibre networks (Enclosures, Cords & Cable) to meet telecom-space demand|Positioned to capture value at the convergence of the Internet of Everything (IoE), Artificial Intelligence, Data Science and Generative AI as new revenue-stream opportunities open up over the next decade|Targeting high-value opportunities in Defense, Education, IT/ITES, E-commerce, Advanced Manufacturing and Digital India initiatives as enterprise project pipelines open up|Leveraging core engineering strengths across Data Centre architectures, fibre deployments and Digital India initiatives to ensure long-term profitable growth|Actively realigning cost structures, eliminating operational redundancies and sharpening productivity to protect operating margins|Combining ongoing pricing strategy adjustments with strict cost-reduction initiatives and an aggressive pipeline of new product introductions to maintain competitive edge|Expanding footprint into fast-growing segments such as high-speed copper and advanced fibre optics to convert product strengths into recurring market wins|Board and Risk Management Committee conduct disciplined worst-case-scenario stress testing to protect the Company's financial foundation|Foresees balancing continued growth in the Enterprise segment against a steady, cautious approach toward the more volatile Telecom sector|Community investment strategy directs targeted spending into healthcare, education and sustainability as part of long-term value creation|Directors recommended a dividend for FY26 subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, and the Board does not propose any transfer to the General Reserve for the year. risks.risk: Raw-material / commodity cost volatility (copper, stainless steel, plastics, fibre)
risks.note: Steep, volatile input-price increases were the primary driver of lower profitability during the year despite revenue growth; the Company relies on staggered price adjustments across product lines to offset this, which carries execution and timing risk.

risks.risk: Change-of-control / ownership transition risk following Amphenol's acquisition of CommScope's CCS business
risks.note: The Company became an indirect majority-owned subsidiary of Amphenol Corporation via a mandatory Open Offer under SEBI SAST Regulations; the transition triggered two Non-Independent Director resignations and two new appointments in the same year, introducing governance and integration uncertainty.

risks.risk: Enterprise network copper business demand deceleration
risks.note: Management flagged a short-term deceleration in this business driven by widespread remote-work adoption and only moderate commercial office-space expansion; offset for now by growth in other segments, but a structural shift in office-space demand could persist.

risks.risk: Telecommunication segment revenue decline tied to lower exports
risks.note: The Telecommunication business declined 15% year-on-year, primarily attributed to lower exports versus the previous financial year, indicating exposure to export-market demand swings.

Company operates against a backdrop of supply chain disruptions, rising interest rates, volatile commodity pricing and evolving regulatory policies, which management says required a structured risk-management framework and conservative financial profile to mitigate.

Macroeconomic caution has caused global enterprise clients to extend project evaluation cycles, resulting in delayed decision-making that can push out or reduce Enterprise/Office Network segment orders.

The Company migrated data storage to a cloud-based system with redundant links across primary and secondary data centres specifically to guard against ransomware and data loss, indicating this was an identified risk area for the business.

The Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, who served for nearly three decades, retired effective May 31, 2026, with a new appointee taking over from June 1, 2026, representing a governance/institutional-knowledge transition.
